_comment: Expected TDX image measurements for the OS images a PROVIDER's broker runs.
This is trust-chain hop 3's allowlist: `attest.BootChainPolicy` compares a
verified provider quote's boot chain against these entries, and with
ZG_GATEWAY_ATTEST_ENFORCE on, a provider whose image is not listed is refused.
SAME SHAPE, DIFFERENT SUBJECT from osimages.json beside it. That file holds the
images the GATEWAY ITSELF is deployed on, for `pcverify -gateway` and the
identity endpoint. This one holds the images the gateway is willing to SEAL
USER PROMPTS TO. Deriving an entry is identical either way, so the whole
procedure lives in osimages.json's header and is not repeated here — read it
before adding anything below. The parser is shared too (evidence.ParseOSImages),
so the same rules hold: 48-byte hex registers, and no all-zero entry.
WHAT AN ENTRY IS WORTH depends entirely on where its values came from. Computed
with dstack-mr from a published release and then confirmed against a live quote,
an entry means 'this enclave boots the OS image we audited'. Copied off a running
provider, it means 'this provider currently reports these registers', which is
the thing being verified and therefore means nothing. There is no way to tell
the two apart by looking at the file, which is why `source` and `page_add` are
recorded per entry and why a reviewer should refuse an entry that cannot say
where it came from.
TWO THINGS AN ENTRY MUST NOT BE. It must not be a DEV image: dstack publishes
`-dev` flavours whose metadata.json carries `is_dev: true`, and they differ from
the production build of the same version only in the rootfs — identical firmware,
kernel and initrd, so ONLY RTMR2 distinguishes them. Listing one grants the whole
fleet whatever a development rootfs carries. And it must not be an image with no
published artifact: without a downloadable release whose digest.txt can be
checked, dstack-mr has nothing independent to run on, so the entry could only
ever have been copied from the deployment.
RECORD THE PAGE-ADD MODE, AND MIND THE NAME. MRTD depends on how the VMM adds
pages during TD build, so it is (image, page-add mode) — the one dimension a
single entry does not cover. Two traps, both hit while writing the first entry:
dstack-mr's option is `two_pass_add_pages` while dstack's vm_config field is
`qemu_single_pass_add_pages`, and tdx.rs feeds one straight into the other WITHOUT
negating it (dstack-mr/src/tdx.rs) — so the names invite writing the mode down
backwards. And when vm_config omits the field entirely, dstack-mr does not assume
single-pass: it takes a default from the QEMU version (machine.rs), false for
>= 9.0 and true for 8.x. Record the mode that actually produced the value, not the
field name you read. A wrong note here does not weaken the check — it sends the
next person to recompute and get a different MRTD, and conclude the entry is
wrong.
ONE ENTRY PER IMAGE, not per provider and not per CVM — attest.BootChain excludes
RTMR0 (VM shape) and RTMR3 (per-instance app events), so many providers on many
machine sizes share one entry. Measured, not assumed, on two axes: a fleet sweep
found eleven providers on one image reporting three distinct RTMR0 values and
identical MRTD/RTMR1/RTMR2; and recomputing this entry across 2G..1024G of memory,
several vCPU counts and QEMU 8.2.0 vs 9.2.1 moved RTMR0 only. The boot chain held
everywhere the page-add mode held.
AN EMPTY LIST MEANS NOT CONFIGURED, and the two modes read it differently:
warn mode proceeds on any image and logs, enforce mode refuses every provider
with ErrMeasurementPolicyNotConfigured — which names the unfinished
configuration rather than blaming the enclave. It never means 'accept anything'.
Fields: `name`, `os_image_hash`, `source` and `page_add` are provenance — which
release this entry was computed from and how — and are never matched on. `mrtd`,
`rtmr1`, `rtmr2` are hex, 48 bytes each, and are the value compared.

images.name: dstack-nvidia-0.5.9
images.page_add: single-pass (two_pass_add_pages=false; vm_config carries no qemu_single_pass_add_pages, so dstack-mr takes its QEMU>=9.0 default)
derivation: 1. Downloaded the release above; `sha256sum -c sha256sum.txt` passed for all
four members, and sha256(sha256sum.txt) equals digest.txt — so digest.txt,
which IS os_image_hash, describes these exact bytes.
2. dstack-mr (Dstack-TEE/dstack 027c62be8c774d806659ca56b5a4e63912b773db)
`diagnose --vm-config <the provider's own vm_config> --image-dir <release>`
computed MRTD/RTMR0/RTMR1/RTMR2 from ovmf.fd, bzImage, initramfs.cpio.gz
and metadata.json's cmdline. No value below was read off the deployment.
3. Compared against a live quote: all four MATCH, RTMR0 included. RTMR0 is not
part of the entry (see attest.BootChain), but its agreeing means the VM
shape is accounted for too, not merely unexamined.
is_dev is false in metadata.json — this is the production flavour.
4. MRTD tracks the page-add mode and nothing else here. Measured as a 2x2:
two_pass=false gives this entry's MRTD under BOTH QEMU 9.2.1 and 8.2.0,
and two_pass=true gives f06dfda6... under both. What the QEMU version does
change is RTMR0 (through `pic`), and RTMR0 is excluded by design — so this
entry does NOT implicitly pin a QEMU version. Memory (2G..1024G) and vCPU
count move nothing in the boot chain either.

images.name: dstack-nvidia-0.5.4.1
images.page_add: single-pass (dstack-mr two_pass_add_pages=false — the mode that reproduces the live quote's MRTD; two_pass_add_pages=true gives f06dfda6… instead, see step 4)
derivation: 1. Downloaded the release above. `sha256sum -c sha256sum.txt` passed for all
four members, and sha256(sha256sum.txt) equals digest.txt — which IS the
os_image_hash above, so these bytes are that release.
2. dstack-mr (Dstack-TEE/dstack 027c62be8c774d806659ca56b5a4e63912b773db)
`measure --two-pass-add-pages false metadata.json` computed MRTD/RTMR1/RTMR2
from ovmf.fd, bzImage, initramfs.cpio.gz and metadata.json's cmdline. No
value below was read off a deployment.
3. Compared against what a live broker quote reports (the glm5.3 provider CVM):
all three MATCH, and that quote's RTMR3 os-image-hash event carries the
os_image_hash above, tying the quote to this artifact. RTMR0 was NOT
reproduced — it records the VM shape, which is not published for that CVM,
and it is excluded from the comparison by design (see attest.BootChain).
4. CALIBRATION, so the page-add mode is measured rather than assumed: the same
binary with --two-pass-add-pages true yields MRTD f06dfda6… instead. The two
runs differ in one flag and nothing else.
5. Shape independence, measured on this image: 1 vCPU/2G, 8/32G, 128/1024G with
8 GPUs, 64/512G with 8 GPUs and 4 NVSwitches, QEMU 8.2.0, and hugepages all
give exactly this boot chain. Only RTMR0 moves.
6. NOT covered, and worth knowing before relying on this entry: in dstack-mr
0.6.0 the root_verity flag feeds only the ACPI tables (acpi.rs), so measuring
with --root-verity false leaves MRTD/RTMR1/RTMR2 unchanged and moves RTMR0
alone. Verity is still pinned by the cmdline's dstack.rootfs_hash, which does
reach RTMR2 — but the VMM-side flag does not.
